EXAM: MRI BILATERAL BREASTS WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST

HISTORY: 46-year-old female recently diagnosed with left breast ductal carcinoma in situ.

COMPARISON: Screening mammogram from [REDACTED] diagnostic mammogram and breast ultrasound from
[REDACTED] stereotactic core biopsy from [REDACTED]. Screening mammogram from 2021, 2022, 2023.

TECHNIQUE: Images were acquired on a GE HDx 3T MRI with a dedicated breast array coil. Sagittal fat suppressed
T2 weighted images were acquired (TR5167, TE99, FA90, 256 x 256 matrix, 4 mm slice thickness). Sagittal FSE T1
weighted images were acquired (TR500, TE18, FA90, 512 x 512, 5 mm slice thickness). Bilateral sagittal T1 weighted
images were acquired (TR433, TE9, 4 mm slice thickness). Sagittal fat suppressed Vibrant gradient echo images were
acquired through both breasts both before and after dynamic intravenous administration of gadolinium (TR7, TE2, TI6,
FA10, Matrix 256 x 256, 2.8 mm slice thickness). These images were acquired dynamically out to 8 minutes. After the
dynamic sagittal imaging, high resolution axial Vibrant images (TR6, TE2, TI18, FA10, Matrix 512 x 512, 1.4 mm slice
thickness) were acquired. Images were reviewed utilizing breast MR software which includes subtraction post
processing and enhancement curve analysis. Computer assisted diagnosis (CAD) was used. 20 ml of Clariscan was
injected from a 20 ml single use vial.
